text: Bullard Mountain is a 4,225-foot (1,288 m) summit in the Boundary Ranges of Alaska, situated immediately east of the terminus of Mendenhall Glacier within Tongass National Forest, 9 mi (14 km) north-northwest of Juneau and 6 mi (10 km) northeast of Juneau International Airport. McGinnis Mountain is located 3.7 mi (6 km) on the opposite side of the glacier, and Heintzleman Ridge is 2.75 mi (4 km) to the south. The mountain is frequently viewed and photographed alongside Mount Wrather, a 5,968-foot (1,819 m) summit 3.9 mi (6 km) to the north, as they appear together in the background behind Mendenhall Lake, a well-known tourist and recreation area. Despite its modest elevation, the mountain has significant relief due to its rise from nearly sea-level Mendenhall Lake in less than two miles. Precipitation runoff from Bullard Mountain flows into the lake through Nugget Creek and Nugget Falls. The mountain is named after Benjamin Bullard (1848–1933), a mining engineer who, in 1907, began mining on Nugget Creek and later constructed a hydroelectric power plant there. According to the Köppen climate classification, Bullard Mountain lies in a subarctic climate zone characterized by cold, snowy winters and mild summers, with temperatures occasionally dropping below −20 °C and wind chill factors falling below −30 °C. This climate supports the presence of the Mendenhall Glacier to the mountain's west, and July is considered the best month for viewing and climbing the peak.
